properties.decision: UNSETTLED. dev_storyflow's most-wanted ask, 2026-08-08: express "this capability needs a surface where a person (or an upstream system) actually writes the data it consumes", so a capability that is realized, built and rendering — but dead because nothing ever writes its input — is caught by a detector rather than by three people producing three wrong root causes. Shapes worth weighing rather than a recommendation: (a) a new edge — cap FED_BY ifc/Actor — with an unrealized_input_path gap when a capability that consumes a field has no writer; (b) a property on the Capability (`needs_input_path: true`) with the detector reading it, which is cheaper and weaker because nothing forces the flag; (c) generalise the existing INTERACTS_WITH by adding a `required` property, so "an actor interacts with this" can become "this does not function unless an actor does"; (d) decline it as out of scope, on the ground that reflow2 models the design and not the operational data path. NOTE WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH: req:the-store-is-reachable-from-a-session says "a capability nothing can call is not delivered — the content store needs a surface", which is exactly this insight scoped to ONE capability and written by hand; nothing generalises it and nothing detects it.
properties.name: OPEN — should a capability be able to declare that it needs a human INPUT path, so that the absence of one is DETECTABLE rather than diagnosable only by three people failing?
properties.rationale: Recorded because it is the one thing the fleet said would have saved the most time, and because it is a VOCABULARY question rather than a detector bug — detect_gaps structurally cannot ask about a surface the design has no way to say is required, which is req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots in its sharpest instance to date. Left `proposed` deliberately: every shape above changes the schema or the detector set, and which one is right is Anthony's call, not a field report's. The evidence is fact:defect-a-realized-capability-can-be-dead-for-want-of-an-input-path.
